column1: # Works from the top-100 list that Russian Wikisource carries and the shelf
# did not. Columns: slug, Wikisource page, author, title, category, blurb.
# Add a row and re-run:  python3 tools/add_wikisource.py --list tools/top100/wanted.tsv
# A page beginning "@" is a collection index: the stories are separate
# Wikisource pages and the tool reads the index's links, in order.
# Two rows are marked SKIP and stay that way until Wikisource has them as a
# book rather than as scattered pages:
#   Басни (Крылов)  — the index links 200 fables as 200 separate pages, and
#                     bleeds into the rest of Krylov's verse.
#   Пётр Первый     — Wikisource's "Пётр I (Толстой)" is A. N. Tolstoy's PLAY,
#                     not the novel; the novel is not there.

column6: A Petersburg gentleman who cannot bring himself to get out of bed is roused by an old schoolfriend and by a young woman who believes she can change him.
In a glass city a thousand years from now, the builder of the state's first spaceship keeps a diary, and a woman with a sharp smile begins to take an interest in him.
A German officer who never gambles hears that an old countess once won three cards in a single night, and sets out to learn her secret.
A former marshal of the nobility learns that his mother-in-law sewed the family jewels into one of a set of twelve chairs, and takes a charming confidence man as his partner in finding it.
A landowner walks the fields and forests of Orel province with his gun, and the serfs, bailiffs and small gentry he meets along the way tell him their lives.
A Georgian boy raised in a monastery escapes into the mountains during a storm, and three days later is found half dead and made to explain himself.
The winter of 1918 in Kiev, where a family of officers and their friends hold to the old order as the city changes hands around them.
On her name day a princess receives a garnet bracelet from the anonymous clerk who has written to her for years, and her husband and brother decide to put a stop to it.
Called to serve on a jury, a prince recognises the prostitute in the dock as the girl he seduced years before, and follows her sentence to Siberia.
A railwayman's son thrown out of school for a prank grows up through the civil war into a Bolshevik who will not stop working even as his body fails.
Village tales from Ukraine, told by a beekeeper: a blacksmith who rides the devil to Petersburg for a pair of slippers, a drowned girl, a witch, a lost letter.
A sailor's daughter in a hostile fishing village is told by a wandering storyteller that a ship with scarlet sails will one day come for her, and she believes it.
The great schemer returns, this time on the trail of an underground Soviet millionaire who lives on a clerk's salary to avoid attention.
Boris takes the throne over the body of a murdered child, and years later a runaway monk crosses into Poland claiming to be that child, alive.
A brutish provincial family schemes to marry off a rich orphan to one of their own, while their idle son fails at every lesson his tutors set him.
A romantic young man arrives in Petersburg full of verses and high feeling, and is taken in hand by a coolly practical uncle in the civil service.
The English present the tsar with a clockwork flea, and a squinting left-handed gunsmith from Tula is set the task of going one better.
A young writer in Petersburg takes in an orphaned girl fleeing her grandfather's house, and is drawn into the ruin of the family he grew up with.
The chronicle of the town of Glupov and the governors sent to rule it, among them one with a music box in place of a head.
A Chechen commander at odds with Shamil goes over to the Russians, and finds himself a guest, a prize and a hostage at once.
A landowner comes home from Paris after his wife's betrayal, and falls in love with a devout young cousin before news arrives that changes everything.
A peasant girl selling flowers near the Simonov monastery meets a young nobleman, and believes he means to keep his word.
A traveller between the two capitals stops at each posting station and sets down what serfdom looks like from the road — the book that sent its author to Siberia.
By the sea in Bessarabia an old woman tells three stories: the son of an eagle, her own many lovers, and the man who tore out his heart to light a way through the forest.
The making of a tsar and a country, from a boy's terror in the Kremlin during the streltsy revolt to the founding of a city in a swamp.
A huge monk on a boat tells his fellow passengers how he got there: a coachman, a horse doctor, a captive among the Tatars, a soldier, and now this.
A beautiful girl with no dowry agrees to marry a petty official, and then the man who abandoned her comes back to town.
In a summer village outside Moscow a band of boys secretly does the heavy work for the families of men away at the front, and the local toughs try to stop them.
A merchant's youngest daughter asks for nothing but a scarlet flower, and her father picks one from a garden that belongs to someone.
The youngest and silliest of three brothers catches a mare and is given a small humpbacked horse, which turns out to be the best friend a fool ever had.
The fables every Russian child learns by heart: the crow and the fox, the dragonfly and the ant, the quartet of animals who cannot work out why they sound so bad.
Twelve Red Guardsmen march through a blizzard in revolutionary Petrograd, and someone is walking ahead of them in the snow.
